case_name: Magnet CTF 2020 — Google Takeout (Chester Russell, spear-phishing with PyInstaller CV malware)
description: Google Takeout export from Chester Russell (king.chester.802@gmail.com), Champlain College cybersecurity student, Google Pixel 3. Three convergent MALICE clusters: (1) Android exploitation research campaign starting Jan 25 2020 (Metasploit, Magisk hidden root, system partition modification); (2) pre-travel OPSEC implementation Mar 5-6 (Magisk, camera metadata stripping 'camera app no metadata Android', app encryption) immediately before Norway trip; (3) spear-phishing attack Mar 23 against Warren Hamilton using fake identity 'Chestnut Russman' and PyInstaller Python malware Chestnut_CV.exe (7.9943 bits/byte entropy, Google API C2 via googleapiclient/httplib2). Accomplice 'Mastermind (Alan Brunswick)' listed in device contacts with email abrunswick8675309@gmail.com, shared payload via Google Drive. Active concealment at every layer: hidden root, fake persona, malware masquerading as CV, Google-domain C2. Verdict: MALICE.

peirce_chain.firstness: My Activity/Search Jan 25: 'how do i hack on an android' → 'metasploit guide' → 'kali msfconsole' → 'install metasploit debian'. Mar 5 midnight: 'adbd insecure', 'root pixel 3', Magisk Manager APK from topjohnwu GitHub. Mar 6: 'camera app no metadata Android', 'encrypt an app', 'cm locker'. Mar 23 19:52: email to warrenhamiltonfinance@gmail.com as 'Chestnut Russman': 'I have the file super encrypted with 6 layers of NSA encryption encodings'. Mar 24 01:47: Alan Brunswick shared Chestnut_CV.exe via Google Drive. Contacts: 'Mastermind (Alan)' = abrunswick8675309@gmail.com. Chestnut_CV.exe: PE32+ x86-64, 26,895,731 bytes, 7.9943 bits/byte, PyImport_AddModule, google.auth.transport._http_client, googleapiclient.http.
peirce_chain.secondness: New phone received Jan 21 — 4 days later searching 'how do i hack on an android' is not normal student behavior. Magisk specifically hides root from apps and SafetyNet — it does not simply root; it conceals rooting. 'Camera app no metadata Android' is covert photography, not privacy — the timing (evening before Norway departure) is not coincidental. A legitimate CV is PDF or DOCX; an executable file named Chestnut_CV.exe is categorically not. Entropy 7.9943 bits/byte = packed Python runtime (PyInstaller). Google API imports in a CV file are malware C2 infrastructure. 'Mastermind' in a contact label is an operational designation, not a casual nickname.
peirce_chain.thirdness: Three-phase attack: platform preparation (root + OPSEC), field operation (Norway with OPSEC-enabled device, accomplice coordination via Twitter DM), payload delivery (spear-phishing Warren Hamilton using fake identity + malware). Two-actor cell: Alan Brunswick (technical/developer) + Chester Russell (social engineering/delivery). Google API C2 is an advanced evasion technique — Google traffic is not firewalled. Carnegie patterns: Authority (fake Wall Street credentials), False scarcity (URGENT), Liking (flattery of target's 'fine establishment'). Active concealment at every layer satisfies MALICE threshold.

devil_advocate: Chester used his real Gmail address (king.chester.802@gmail.com) for the Warren Hamilton attack — inconsistent with sophisticated OPSEC. The 'Chestnut Russman' persona was immediately recognized as fraudulent. The attack failed. This is a Champlain College cybersecurity student conducting what may be a poorly-executed coursework exercise or authorized CTF (Magnet CTF 2020). Metasploit and Magisk are legitimate tools in security education. Norway trip could be a personal holiday — Finse is famous as a Star Wars filming location, not exclusively a clandestine meeting site. COVID forced early return on March 12, explaining the abbreviated trip.

Contains: My Activity (Search, Chrome, YouTube), Location History (Semantic JSON), Mail (All mail.mbox, 97 emails), Contacts (All Contacts.vcf), Google Play Store (Devices.json), Drive (Chestnut_CV.exe). Primary evidence container for all downstream artifacts.

Shared by Alan Brunswick (abrunswick8675309@gmail.com) via Google Drive to Chester Russell at 2020-03-24T01:47Z. Key strings: PyImport_AddModule, PyImport_ExecCodeModule (PyInstaller markers); google.auth.transport._http_client, googleapiclient.http, httplib2 (Google API C2 channel). Delivered to Warren Hamilton (warrenhamiltonfinance@gmail.com) under social engineering pretext by fake persona 'Chestnut Russman'.

caie_fractures.description: Three independent signals converge on the same attack: (1) Chestnut_CV.exe (malware file with Google API C2) shared by Alan Brunswick via Drive; (2) Warren Hamilton email thread documenting the social engineering and his discovery; (3) Chester's own search history for Alan's Xbox gamertag on the same day as the attack — real-time coordination. Three independent forensic sources confirm a single attack event.

OPSEC implementation (Mar 5-6: Magisk, camera metadata, app encryption) immediately precedes Norway departure (Mar 6-7). The temporal proximity — 12-24 hours between OPSEC setup and departure — is not coincidental. Pattern matches pre-operation preparation: secure the platform before deploying it in the field.
